cases.name: Shannon Leah Hiott
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Shannon will always be a bright star to her parents, family and many friends. The loss to all those that knew her is immeasurable. A champion of change and compassion for all things, Shannon was a proud advocate of women’s rights, equality, mental health care and spay/neuter programs. She was an advocate of sustainable living, and was earth conscious on all levels. Known as a dedicated cat guardian, Shannon took part in the tedious process of TNR- rescuing 7 cats from her own backyard and asking for donations each birthday for cat rescue operations. Custom artwork and creations at her home accentuated her lifelong love of cats: a patio built so her owned-cats could comfortably and safely enjoy being outdoors, heated water bowls in the winter, coolers filled with straw for feral cats in winter and cared for all those she encountered. She was an active member of the local music scene and one of her greatest joys in life was going to music festivals and promoting her favorite bands. Consistently supporting local artists and creatives, she surrounded herself with love and good vibes. No one will forget her love of Halloween and the spectacular costumes she put together from scratch. She was a true force to be reckoned with and mastered countless skills including sewing, clothing-design, makeup artistry, and Pokémon hunting (achieving a level of 35).  Shannon is known as someone thoughtful, generous, silly and tenacious. She graduated from The Ohio State University in 2017 with a Bachelors of Psychology.  Shannon recently accomplished obtaining her Fraud Investigator Certification with Nationwide Insurance Company of which she was most proud and excited about. Shannon’s commitment to self-love, moral integrity, leadership, friendship, and promoting change in the community will leave an everlasting impact on all those who had the honor of knowing her."
cases.narrative: He allegedly stabbed her nearly 40 times.

cases.name: Nicole Sonya "Nikki" Dortch Pannell
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Nicole, widely known as Nikki ... was a beacon of radiance and generosity, known for her effervescent spirit, charisma, and charm. Nikki had a profound impact on everyone she met, making lasting impressions with her love, thoughtful gifts, her quick wit and infectious laugh. She was a brilliant spirit and the void left in her absence will never be filled.

Nikki was educated in the Cleveland Public School system and graduated from Max Hayes High School. She furthered her education at The Ohio State University obtaining her Bachelor’s Degree in Education with a focus in Corporate Training and Development. Her professional life was marked by a series of significant roles where her leadership skills and personality were on full display. She dedicated herself to enhancing organizational growth and personal development at several institutions including Wallick Communities, Rogue Fitness, City of Columbus, and The Ohio State University. Nikki charged up the corporate ladder and left every organization better than it was prior to her arrival. She was also looking forward to starting a graduate program at Case Western Reserve University. Nikki served as a board member for the Central Ohio Association of Talent Development and began her career teaching at Children First. Nikki touched the lives of dozens of children, and this would prove foundational when she entered motherhood herself.

Nikki received her Lord in Savior Jesus Christ in early adulthood and was a committed member of Living Faith Apostolic Church. She was often involved in church activities and cherished her time in fellowship. Her hobbies reflected her vibrant personality, including shooting pool (she was a beast), attending comedy shows, cooking, dancing, and playing cards. She loved everything Cleveland and often traveled back home to watch and attend Browns football games with family. She loved visiting new places, smoking the occasional cigar, dining out, and had a keen interest in fashion and music. Above all, her greatest joy was her son, Ethan, with whom she shared her love for life's adventures."

cases.name: Randelle Denise Bowman
cases.about:
Her obituary said: "Born and raised in the South Side of Columbus, Ohio, she spent the bulk of her life committed to making it a better place for all residents. Randy graduated from Marion Franklin High School in 1976. She continued her high education journey at Capital University where she earned a degree in Social Work.

Randalle loved to celebrate holidays with her family. Christmas was her favorite. She began an annual celebration called Advent which brought everyone together weekly on the month of December and enabled everyone to adopt a spirit of gratitude and hopefulness while centering God as the core of their lives. The tradition has continued for over 30 years. Her giving heart allowed her to open her home to all people and utilized it to serve as a refuge for everyone who found themselves in need. Her giving spirit and generosity was the core of who Randelle was as a person. She loved to dance and sing, travel but above all things, she loved the Lord. Randelle was a faithful member of Resurrection Missionary Baptist Church and former member of Clair United Methodict Church.

She was a dedicated employee of the Southside Settlement House where she was responsible for senior services, community lunch programs, volunteer recruitment coordination, and outpatient drug and alcohol counseling within the community. She also worked as Choices where she provided counseling to families who sought shelter due to abuse. At Care Star, she assisted clients to remain in the least restrictive environments while maintaining their independence. Serving as a treatment coordinator with the National Youth Advocacy Program, Randelle acted as a liaison for foster parents proving linkage for successful treatment coordination, and home placement.

During her time serving her community, Randelle was instrumental in improving the processes and methods for residents to receive government assistance and advocated for a program that brought music to the park (Lions Park). Over the years, her hard work and stanch advocacy earned her several accommodations for the City of Columbus, Randy was a Member of the Ladies of Distinction Inc – Columbus Chapter. Randelle Bowman’s public legacy is largely one of neighborhood service and civic involvement, with over 3 decades of service in the southside area commission and tireless efforts to represent and advocate for residents in her community."
cases.narrative: On 7/11/2026, Bowman's family requested a welfare check after becoming concerned they had not heard from her. While waiting for officers to arrive, relatives said they saw Holmes walk away from the home through the backyard and into a neighboring property. When officers entered the home, investigators say they found Bowman dead in the basement, rolled inside a rug with her throat slit.

cases.name: Shauda Sharrika Starks
cases.about:
Her obituary said: "There are some people whose smile can brighten a room before they ever say a word. Shauda Sharrika "Day Day" Starks was one of those people. Her beautiful smile, caring heart, and love for others made her someone who will always be remembered and forever missed.

She grew up surrounded by family and friends who loved her dearly. She graduated from Midview High School and the Lorain County Joint Vocational School, where she earned her certification in Early Childhood Education. Her passion for children reflected the kindness and nurturing spirit that defined her life. She later became employed with the Ohio Bureau of Motor Vehicles in Columbus, Ohio.

At the heart of Shauda's life was her love for her children. Her greatest joy was found in Nyome Johnson, Michael McAfee III, Mikaizha McAfee, and Darshan Norman Jr. They were the center of her world and the reason behind so much of her strength, determination, and unconditional love. She also shared a special bond with her beloved goddaughter, Ja'liyah Walsh, whom she loved dearly.

Shauda cherished the simple moments that made life meaningful—spending time with family, laughing with friends, celebrating special occasions, and creating memories that will remain in the hearts of those she loved. She had a gentle spirit, a compassionate heart, and a way of making people feel welcomed and cared for. Whether through a warm smile, a listening ear, or a thoughtful act of kindness, she touched countless lives."

Thomasena had a gift for bringing people together. She loved entertaining her family and friends—cooking, listening to music, sharing laughter, and cracking jokes. (A true Southfield trait… if you know, you know.) Her joyful spirit never met a stranger and never made an enemy. She carried a grateful soul, a warm heart, and a light that touched everyone around her.


Thomasena was truly loved by many and will be sorely missed by all who had the blessing of knowing her, including a host of nieces, nephews, extended family, and friends."

cases.name: Tiffany Creech
cases.about:
Family members described Tiffany Creech as funny, caring and deeply connected to her sister. Heather said the two shared matching tattoos and often communicated without words.

“We had our own language,” she said. “I would just look at her and she'd just look at me and we'd just have that look and we'd just start busting out laughing. If you needed something, she would give it to you, if she had it, you just had to ask.”
cases.narrative:
Medics found Creech bleeding and tried to save her life. She was pronounced dead a short time later.

Court records said her live-in boyfriend Michael Johnson struck her with a baseball bat.
